title: Quarterly alignment: sprint threads for Hosted API & Model Catalog
creator: Morgan Lee
description: Goal: produce a concise, executable quarterly plan that maps Hosted API endpoint priorities to model-catalog commitments and sprint lanes. This ticket captures the strategy, decision thresholds, staffing assumptions, and contingency triggers for Q2. The outcome is a published runbook and sprint-level milestones that product, eng, design and SRE can adopt for execution and monitoring. The plan emphasizes: 1) aligning model onboarding windows with capacity hedges; 2) defining canary/rollback windows for model swaps; 3) mapping OKR signals (latency/cost/quality) to release gates; 4) ensuring observability and eval criteria are in place before commit windows.
acceptance_criteria: Cross-functional kickoff held with Engineering, Design, SRE and Research; notes captured in the runbook
Sprint lanes created and added to the Q2 board with owners and estimates
Model-catalog commitments (onboarding + pruning) scheduled with canary windows and fallback models identified
Runbook includes decision thresholds for capacity hedging and a rollback play for critical endpoints
Dashboards and alerting queries for OKR signals (p50/p95 latency, per-token cost, model-quality regressions) linked in the runbook

notes: Trade-off: tighter commit windows reduce drift but increase risk of last-minute capacity shortfalls; plan adopts a conservative 15% hedge for initial swaps.
Decision: prefer model variants with identical tokenization to simplify routing fallback (reduces edge-case decoding regressions).
Follow-up: schedule a micro-sim of traffic migration during sprint 2 with SRE and infra to validate autoscaling policies.
risk_summary: Capacity mismatch if model size/latency differs materially from profile
Quality regressions if eval coverage is insufficient for customer cohorts
Coordination overhead across Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployment owners
